name: St Andrew's Church

layers.essential_history: [[c:St Andrew's is mostly 13th century outside, including its tower. Inside are monuments to Christopher Freeman, who died in 1610, and Parson Nicholas Latham, who died in 1620.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:In 1818 and 1819 Henry Rolls, husband of the poet Mary Rolls, was rector here.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:In the church, the parson's plans for the almshouses lie open. A page is missing, and someone has written on the next page in a backwards hand.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:Backwards writing]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Whose name is it? (surname)]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:NROHT backwards is THORN, the start of THORNE. The lawyer was here.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]

evidence: [[c:THORN is written backwards in the parson's book.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Head west, about 50 metres as the crow flies, to the old rectory.  Keep to pavements and public paths.]]
